ops.title: apple-container vmnet NAT breaks on container deletes — recover with `container system restart`
ops.body:
**Operational lesson (2026-07-18/19, live incident on the yclaw host).**

Deleting apple `container`s (`container delete <name>`) can silently break the **shared vmnet NAT** for the `default` network (192.168.72.0/24), leaving every container on it with **no outbound path** while the runtime still reports `status: running`.

**Symptoms (all observed):**
- Host: no route to `192.168.72.0/24` (`netstat -rn` shows only the fleet's 192.168.64.x on bridge100), and `ping 192.168.72.1` (the container gateway) = 100% loss.
- Inside a container: tailscale can't reach `controlplane.tailscale.com` / DERP (`no route to host`, `network is unreachable`), DNS to the subnet gateway `192.168.72.1:53` times out → tailscale never comes up → can't reach `metal` → model plane down.
- `container network ls` still lists the network; `container system status` = running. So the runtime looks healthy — the break is the vmnet gateway/NAT beneath it.
- Restarting just the affected container does NOT fix it (the fresh container gets a new .72.x IP but still can't reach the gateway).

**Root cause:** the trigger here was deleting the `e3-probe`/`e3-probe-int` prototype containers (on the e3-egress/e3-internal nets); tearing down their vmnet interfaces glitched the shared vmnet. The `e3-egress`/`e3-internal` **networks** survive the container delete (only the containers go).

**Fix (verified):** `container system stop && container system start`. This re-creates the vmnet bridge (a fresh `bridge101` picked up `192.168.72.x`, host route restored), and outbound egress + tailscale + metal come back. Cost: **all containers stop** — supervised ones (com.yclaw.container-hermes recreates hermes in ~5s) come back; **unsupervised containers do NOT auto-restart** and must be recreated by their owner.

**Guidance:** before deleting apple-containers on a shared host, expect a possible NAT glitch; keep `container system restart` in hand. Don't attribute a container→metal outage to tailscale/pf until you've checked the host route to the container subnet.
